text:
maya: Quick design check — the new control in the pool picker labeled "Handoff to pool" is getting confused reactions in yesterday's usability test. screenshots in thread.
sam (PM): saw that. People expect either "Move" or "Switch pool". "Handoff" felt vague.
liam (Frontend): from an implementation POV, we also have the microstate where the request is queued to the other pool vs actually migrated — need clarity in copy and loading states.
frances (A11y): also flagged keyboard focus order. When you open the dropdown, the Handoff button jumps tab focus. That breaks keyboard flow.
anya (UX Research): in test 4/12 participants used "switch" language 7/12 times, "migrate" 3/12, "handoff" 2/12. Quote: "Handoff sounds like throwing it over a fence." :grimacing:
oliver (ML Infra): important nuance — some workloads are pinned (dedicated), some are eligible for burst move. Copy needs to reflect eligibility, otherwise support tickets.
maya: proposed updates: label -> "Move workload to pool"; secondary caption -> "Eligible for burst: Yes/No"; confirmation modal: show ETA and if KV cache invalidates.
sam (PM): I like explicitness. Can we keep a short single-line label and a helper text rather than nested modals? Less interruption for power users.
liam (Frontend): helper text is fine. For the button aria-label I'd recommend: `aria-label="Move workload to <pool-name>. Opens migration options."`
frances (A11y): prefer to avoid "opens" in aria-labels. Better: `aria-label="Move workload to <pool-name>. Migration options available."` Also ensure `role=dialog` announced when modal appears.
maya: noted — will update mocks. Also thinking about the SLO slider guardrail: when you push min very low and burst high, the copy should warn about potential latency spikes.
anya (UX Research): participants didn't notice the tiny tooltip. We should surface a persistent shelf message when config combinations are risky (inline, non-modal).
sam (PM): +1 for shelf message. Example copy: "Warning: burst settings may increase tail latency for this route. Recommended: keep min >= 2 for steady traffic. Learn more."
liam (Frontend): shelf can be a live region for screen readers: `aria-live="polite"` so updates are announced when values change.
frances (A11y): confirm that the slider handles have accessible names and keyboard increments match the stepper values. 1 GPU step is large — offer fine-grain keyboard adjustments (e.g., Ctrl+arrow) as an optional enhancement.
maya: UX question: should we inline the pool tag (e.g., "gpu-pool: high-priority") into the confirmation copy? It helps trust.
oliver (ML Infra): yes, include pool metadata (region, instance type, capacity class) in the confirmation so operators know where it lands. Also show fallback policy (if target pool is full).
sam (PM): legal/enterprise ask: when data residency matters, make pool region visible earlier — maybe a small flag in the picker item: "EU (compliant)".
liam (Frontend): small UI nit — when switching selections, the list reorders which causes focus to move. Keep stable ordering or trap focus until selection settles.
maya: actionable list I'll push to the figma file: 1) change label to "Move workload to pool"; 2) add inline helper text; 3) persistent shelf warning for risky SLO combos; 4) confirmation shows pool metadata + ETA + fallback; 5) a11y keyboard shortcuts and aria-live for shelf; 6) stable ordering in pool list.
frances (A11y): please include a small checklist for testing with VoiceOver and NVDA in the PR description.
anya (UX Research): I'll attach the full test quotes and the heatmap of where people clicked — very useful for copy tone.
liam (Frontend): I can prototype the aria-live shelf and keyboard modifiers. ETA: EOW for a lightweight build.
oliver (ML Infra): I'll add a server-side flag for "migration-allowed" and return a reason code when disallowed so UI can render the exact helper copy.
maya: thanks — once liam's prototype is ready can we run a 5-user follow-up before we push to canary?
sam (PM): yes — schedule a quick validation sprint. @deploy-bot any conflicts with upcoming releases?
deploy-bot: Heads up: there's a planned infra deploy tomorrow 02:00 UTC that touches pool APIs. Recommend feature branch protected until deploy completes. :warning:
maya: noted, we'll hold the merged PR until after that window. thanks all :thumbsup:
